subject: Pilot success criteria & signoff runway
messages:
From: Asha Banerjee <asha@healthgrid.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elliot Tanner <elliot.t@healthgrid.io>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot success criteria & signoff runway

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week — the team at HealthGrid is keen to run a short pilot of Redwood to validate inference latency and clinical concordance on a 10k-case extrapolation. Before we commit resources we want a short mutual action plan that lays out acceptance tests and clear exit gates. High-level asks from our side: 

- A concise success definition we can show execs (ops + clinical).
- Concrete pass/fail acceptance tests (smoke + regression) we can run against our sample dataset.
- A go/no-go window and signoff owners.

Target timeline: 6-week pilot start mid-August if we can agree signoff criteria this month. Can you send a simple MAP + test inventory that includes the metrics we should expect (latency P95, token cost estimates, concordance thresholds) and any rollback triggers?

Thanks —
Asha
Asha Banerjee
Director of Product, HealthGrid
[attachment: sample_data_manifest.csv]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Banerjee <asha@healthgrid.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot success criteria & signoff runway

Hi Asha — great to hear this aligns with your schedule. Attached is a first-draft MAP (spreadsheet) and a short acceptance-test catalogue. Key points up front: 

1) Success definition (single sentence): "Redwood integration reduces inference latency to <=200ms P95 on production-like traffic while maintaining >=92% clinical concordance against HealthGrid's human-annotated reference set for the pilot scope."

2) Three-tier acceptance tests (smoke, functional/regression, performance):
   - Smoke: model responds to canonical prompts, no runtime errors, correct schema for structured outputs.
   - Regression: sample of 1,000 labeled cases, concordance >=92% (precision/recall table included).
   - Performance: end-to-end P95 latency <=200ms (single-request baseline) and cost estimate within budget bucket (we'll show per-1000-token math).

3) Exit gates / go-no-go windows:
   - Soft-go (week 2): pass smoke + demo to clinical owners.
   - Hard acceptance (week 5): pass regression + performance thresholds. Failure here triggers a block/rollback plan with remediation tasks and a re-test window of 2 weeks.

4) Roles & signoff:
   - HealthGrid signoff: Asha (Product), Elliot (Clinical Ops).
   - Redwood signoff: Marissa (CS Lead), Tessa (SE owner), Karthik (Performance).

5) Next steps: 
   - We need your sample dataset access (S3 link or share this sheet) and confirmation on which 10k cases map to the labeled subset for regression.
   - Karthik will add a short, prioritized test inventory and the exact measurement plan.

I've attached MAP_HG_v1.xlsx (outline + milestone dates) and a lightweight acceptance_test_matrix.csv. If that looks fine, propose we lock criteria by Friday and run a kickoff week of Aug 10.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: MAP_HG_v1.xlsx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Banerjee <asha@healthgrid.io>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot success criteria & signoff runway

Thanks — adding the measurement plan and concrete test definitions below. Please see the attached CSV for the full matrix. I'll summarize critical items here so the execs have something quick to read.

Measurement plan (what we will measure, how, and pass threshold):
- Latency: end-to-end P95 measured over a 4-hour window with pilot traffic (simulated client at 30 RPS). PASS if P95 <= 200ms.
- Throughput: sustained tokens/sec >= baseline required for your dashboard workload (we will run target QPS test). PASS if 1-minute sustained throughput >= target.
- Concordance (clinical label agreement): measured on a 1,000-case labeled holdout. PASS if overall agreement >= 92% and no critical pathology class has recall < 85%.
- Determinism/regression: training of prompt templates + seed checking; PASS if >= 99% schema stability and no unapproved hallucination classes observed above 2% frequency in the sample.

Acceptance tests (high priority):
1) Smoke test (Day 1): API auth, schema, basic prompt sanity.
2) Regression batch (Week 3): run 1k labeled cases, produce confusion matrix, per-class recall/precision, and a short summary doc.
3) Latency run (Week 4): 4-hour P95 run. Collect traces and p95 distribution by endpoint.
4) Cost estimate and token accounting (Week 4): per-request token burn and projected monthly cost at scaled volume.

Exit gates and remediation sequences: 
- If smoke fails: block and triage within 48 hours (owner: Tessa).
- If regression fails but latency passes: pause rollout, open a quality remediation sprint (owner: HealthGrid + Redwood), re-run regression after fixes; re-test window = 14 days.
- If latency fails (P95 >200ms) but regression passes: performance tuning + temporary routing to a fallback model (lower cost but higher latency). Recovery plan must be executed within 7 days to continue pilot.
- If both regression and latency fail: escalate to execs for disposition (possible contract pause).

Attachments: acceptance_test_matrix.csv (columns: test_id,test_type,owner,pass_threshold,method,notes)

I'll also include suggested smoke scripts and a short Jupyter notebook for running the regression analysis once we have dataset access.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: acceptance_test_matrix.csv]

From: Elliot Tanner <elliot.t@healthgrid.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Banerjee <asha@healthgrid.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot success criteria & signoff runway

Tessa/Karthik — thank you for the clear plan and test definitions. This is exactly what the steering committee asked for. A few quick answers and confirmations from HealthGrid: 

- We will share S3 access to the 10k pilot set by EOD Monday (access grant request already in motion).
- We agree to the pass thresholds you proposed; two minor asks: can you add a short check for per-case explanation length (we need a max token budget per explanation) and a sampling strategy for rare pathology classes so recall is meaningfully estimated?
- Timeline: kickoff Aug 10 (week 0 smoke), regression run week 3, performance window week 4, final signoff week 5. If all passes, procurement will issue a PO in the next business week.

We accept the remediation windows and escalation ladder. Please send a one-page decision rack we can present to execs (summary: criteria, signoff owners, timeline). If you send that today we can put it on Friday's steering deck.

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff.

Elliot Tanner
VP Clinical Ops, HealthGrid
